blocks.text: That the dove is here said to nest in the sides of the mouth of the hole, Gussetius, in his Lexicon p. 573, refers to the fact that doves are not accustomed to place their nest directly opposite the opening, but to one side or the other of the opening; hence those who build dovecotes open the windows of the cells not in their middle but at the outer edge of the face. But I much prefer the opinion of Grotius, who understands the words עברי פי - פחת of the sides [II, 546] of a split rock. The guesses of the ancient interpreters, which contribute nothing to understanding the meaning, have been listed by J. D. Michaelis in Observatt. Critt. et Philologg. ad Ierem. p. 256.

I wholeheartedly agree with Bochart in saying that the words יונה אלם רחוקים are the beginning of a song to whose tune David composed this Psalm (what we noted above, at vol. 1, book 3, ch. 17, note 8, about a similar custom of the Syrians in titling songs should be recalled here); but in explaining the words themselves one would labour in vain today. For who could draw a sound meaning from the words Sey Lob und Ehr, which are found written above many hymns, unless he knew the first line of the song whose tune is prescribed? We may therefore remain ignorant of the sense of those three Hebrew words without loss. Yet no one would readily deny the conjecture put forward by Bochart the praise of acuteness, especially if one compares it with the trifles other interpreters have produced about these much-vexed words, which, if one wishes, can be read gathered together in Pfeiffer's Dubia Vexata p. 605, further in Simonis' Lex. Hebr. under the words אלם and עלם, and in J. B. Koehler's Animadverss. Critt. on Psal. LVI. 1. in the Repertorium für bibl. und morgenl. Litterat., edited by Eichhorn, vol. 8, p. 252 ff.
